# Holotope.js

> TypeScript toolkit for accountable higher-dimensional geometry: authoritative
> R^N state, explicit projection or slicing, traceable source identity, and
> source-space simulation. Experimental API; target ES modules.

## Read this first

- README.md — installation, package overview, runnable public examples.
- docs/learn/mental-model.md — package responsibilities and the source → representation → interaction loop.
- docs/learn/experiment-documents.md — safe declarative experiment intake and current runtime boundary.
- docs/learn/source-retained-dimension-bridge.md — the complete typed pipeline:
  one authoritative R4 body, a rigid model, three views, render products, and an
  honest pick. Start here for the minimum end-to-end composition.
- docs/learn/cookbook.md — verified task-oriented snippets.
- docs/learn/representation-provenance.md — what a pick can and cannot recover.
- docs/learn/representation-claims.md — reading a pick as one claim instead of two fields.
- docs/learn/physics/ — rigid mechanics, contact capability boundaries, and RN XPBD
  (index page maps the seven task pages).

## Package map

- `@holotope/core`: zero-dependency Float64 N-D math, geometry, polytopes,
  projections, slicing, source references, fields, lattices, spectral analysis.
- `@holotope/physics`: headless R4 rigid bodies and RN point/XPBD systems.
  It never renders and it does not automatically make all registered rigid
  bodies collide.
- `@holotope/experiment-physics`: the physics model capability; compiles
  `physics.model.rigid4` descriptors into live R4 rigid bodies driven by a
  document-level integer step clock. Depends on core, physics, experiment.
- `@holotope/experiment`: inert, versioned experiment documents with bounded
  JSON intake, semantic validation, canonical SHA-256 identity, stable
  dependency planning, and headless explicit-capability compilation of
  sources -- `core.source.hypercube` and `core.source.hyperrectangle`, the
  latter taking one full edge length per ambient axis for a centered orthotope
  whose topology is the hypercube's -- models, and
  coordinate/perspective/section representations into a
  registry of live objects with derived lineage. It owns live parameter
  reads/writes, bounded action invocation, stamped observations, exact CPU
  snapshots, traces, and replay. A `probe` action reports `sourceCellStatus`
  on every path — the reasoned outcome, never an omitted field — with
  `sourceCell` present exactly when it is `'resolved'`, and
  `sourceCellPrecision` (`'exact'` or `'renderer'`) naming which bound
  resolved it. `'renderer'` names the bound, not the provenance of the input
  point, and a projection still cannot manufacture a unique source point. Presentation panes remain document metadata
  for renderer adapters.
- `@holotope/three`: Three.js peer-dependency adapters. Products expose an
  ordinary `.object` and must be updated from authoritative source state.
- `@holotope/three/webgpu`: optional WebGPU/TSL realization paths. Preserve
  the Float64 CPU path for validation and source-space semantics.

## Non-negotiable model rules

1. Keep the source in R^N. Do not simulate or edit the projected Three mesh as
   though it were the source object.
2. Projection can be ambiguous; an exact slice is a different observation.
3. A `RepresentationHitN` reports three independent things: `source` identity,
   point precision (`ambientPointStatus`), and uniqueness (`ambiguity`).
   `ambientPointStatus: 'exact'` means exact on the selected source primitive,
   not unique under the map. Claim **the** source point only when
   `ambiguity === 'none'`.
4. `RigidBody4` / `PhysicsWorld4` and `XpbdParticleN` / `XpbdWorldN` are
   separate simulation layers.
5. All R4 vectors use `[x, y, z, w]`. R4 bivectors use
   `[xy, xz, xw, yz, yw, zw]` = `[01, 02, 03, 12, 13, 23]`.

## Primary imports

```ts
// @holotope/core
import {
  VecN, MatN, BivectorN, Rotor4, TransformN,
  CellComplex, createHypercube, createHyperrectangle,
  cellComplexBoundsAlongAxisN, cellComplexBoundsAlongDirectionN,
  tetrahedralizeCuboidCells,
  PerspectiveProjection, CoordinateProjection, HyperplaneSlice4,
  PlaneEmbedding3D
} from '@holotope/core';

// @holotope/physics
import {
  massPropertiesFromCellComplex4, RigidBody4, PhysicsWorld4,
  XpbdParticleN, XpbdWorldN, compileXpbdParticleBindingN,
  compileXpbdParticleHyperplaneFamilyN, predictXpbdInertialStateN,
  evaluateXpbdPotentialStateN, evaluateXpbdIncrementalPotentialN,
  compileXpbdIncrementalPotentialProblemN,
  searchXpbdIncrementalPotentialArmijoN,
  minimizeXpbdIncrementalPotentialN,
  recoverXpbdIncrementalPotentialFeasibleBaseN,
  xpbdMassPreconditionedDirectionN,
  xpbdSteepestDescentDirectionN,
  applyXpbdIncrementalPotentialResultN,
  stepXpbdIncrementalPotentialN,
  stepXpbdIncrementalPotentialWorldN,
  compileXpbdSourceSimplexAabbHierarchyN
} from '@holotope/physics';

// @holotope/three
import {
  ProjectedEdges3D, ProjectedSurface3D, SlicedComplex3D, SectionChart3D,
  DragRotation4D,
  representationHitFromProjectedEdge,
  representationHitFromProjectedSurface,
  representationHitFromSectionChart,
  representationHitFromSlicedComplex
} from '@holotope/three';

// @holotope/experiment
import {
  parseExperimentJsonV0, validateExperimentDocumentV0,
  prepareExperimentDocumentV0, compileExperimentDocumentV0,
  coreExperimentCompilerV0
} from '@holotope/experiment';

// @holotope/experiment-physics
import { physicsExperimentCompilerV0 } from '@holotope/experiment-physics';
```

For untrusted experiment text, call `parseExperimentJsonV0()` before object
validation; a retained JavaScript object cannot expose duplicate JSON keys
discarded by an earlier parser. Descriptors are authored recipes, not runtime
objects or `RepresentationLineageN`. `prepareExperimentDocumentV0()` returns a
copied, deeply frozen, canonically hashed document.
`compileExperimentDocumentV0(prepared, { compilers:
[coreExperimentCompilerV0(), physicsExperimentCompilerV0()] })` then
constructs live source, model, and representation objects behind a registry
that owns every runtime experiment id. Capabilities are explicit caller
values, never a global registry, and a kind without a supplied capability is a
typed `capability-unavailable` refusal rather than a partial compilation.
Representation lineage is derived from the constructed projection or slice,
so a compiled experiment can never report `custom-projection`. Discover the
live surface through `listParameters()`, `readParameter()`, `listActions()`,
`listObservations()`, `invoke()`, and `observe()`. Presentation panes remain
on `compilation.document`; they are validated metadata, not headless registry
objects.

## Core anchors

- Vectors/transforms: `VecN`, `MatN`, `BivectorN`, `Rotor4`, `TransformN`.
- Rotation queries/sampling: `Rotor4.principalAnglesBetween(a, b)` returns the
  two physical invariant-plane angles; `Rotor4.geodesicDistanceBetween(a, b)`
  is their norm and remains defined where `log()` is non-unique;
  `Rotor4.random(rng?)` samples Haar-uniform SO(4), unlike a uniform bivector.
- Topology: `CellComplex` (`cellsOfDim`, `cellCount`, `vertexCount`,
  `getPosition` returning a bare `Float64Array`, `groups` of
  `{ dim, verticesPerCell, kind, indices }` with no cell count of their own),
  cuboid tetrahedralization, source-cell references.
- Hand authoring: `new CellComplex(ambientDim, packedFloat64Positions,
  cellGroups)` is the strict public constructor. It retains the typed arrays,
  validates indices, and does not infer missing edge/face groups. See the
  cookbook's literal-authoring recipe; do not invent a `{ dim, positions,
  cells }` object shape.
- Slice ranges: `cellComplexBoundsAlongDirectionN(complex, slice.normal,
  transform?)` returns the vertex-hull offset interval in source or transformed
  space. It does not promise every offset inside a non-convex/disconnected
  source produces a non-empty section.
- Parent-cell provenance: `tetrahedralizeCuboidCells` is additive and drops the
  parent map; `simplexizeCuboidGroupN` returns `simplexGroup` beside
  `sourceCellIndices` and `permutationIndices`, parallel arrays indexed by
  output-simplex ordinal.
- Headless slicing: `sliceTetrahedra` (3 numbers per vertex) and
  `sliceTetrahedraAmbient` (4) take
  `(positions, indices, slice, out)` and return the vertex count written; size
  `out` for six vertices per tetrahedron.
- Dimension-generic sections: `HyperplaneSliceN` is the affine chart in any RN
  (`ambientDim` inferred from its normal, `chartDim = ambientDim - 1`,
  `axisAligned(ambientDim, hiddenAxis, offset)`, `signedDistance(point)` taking
  one array rather than R4's four scalars), and `sectionSimplexGroupN` cuts a
  group of simplicial k-cells with it into `(k-1)`-simplices.
  **A section is an intersection, not a projection.** A projection is
  many-to-one, so an image point does not name a source point; a section is
  injective on what it keeps and loses dimension instead. Non-simplicial input
  is a typed refusal telling you to simplexize — no topology is guessed. Cells
  with no vertex strictly below the plane are suppressed rather than emitted,
  and `diagnostics` distinguishes suppressed from empty. Every output vertex
  carries `lineage`, a CSR sparse affine combination of **original** source
  vertices, which is what a single source edge plus a parameter cannot do: pass
  a previous section's `lineage` back in and an R5 → R4 → R3 chain still names
  R5 vertices rather than the intermediate complex's.
- Rendering an RN section: `SectionChart3D(complex, group, slice, options?)`
  from `@holotope/three` draws the section in its own chart — points for
  0-cells, segments for 1-cells, coherently wound double-sided triangles for
  2-cells — with exactly one section evaluation per `update(transform?)`, the
  immutable result observable as `.section` (diagnostics included, so an empty
  draw range is never a guess), and refusals by name for charts above
  dimension 3. A caller-supplied `material` is never disposed by the product.
  `representationHitFromSectionChart(product, intersection)` resolves a picked
  primitive to its parent source cell exactly, carries each corner's affine
  ancestry (original vertices even through a chained render), and reports the
  embedded ambient point as `'approximate'` — Float32 display coordinates
  qualify a point, they do not upgrade it.
- Reading a pick: `describeRepresentationHitN` returns one claim
  (`unique`, `on-selected-primitive`, `approximate`, `unavailable`) instead of
  leaving `ambientPointStatus` and `ambiguity` to be combined by hand.
- Observation: `PerspectiveProjection`, `CoordinateProjection`,
  `OrthographicProjection`, `HyperplaneSlice4`, `HyperplaneSliceN`, inverse
  fibres and map lineage. R2 content displays through `PlaneEmbedding3D` —
  an injective `DisplayMap3D`, not a `Projection`: `[x, y] → [x, y, 0]`
  exactly, `invertPoint` returning the unique preimage on the image or a
  typed `off-image` status, no fibre. Render products accept any
  `DisplayMap3D`; hits through an embedding report `ambiguity: 'none'` and a
  renderer-derived inverse stays `'approximate'`.
- Fields: quaternion and bicomplex Julia evaluators, generic samples and
  isosurface records.
- Scientific structures: regular polychora, Coxeter/Wythoff construction,
  exact-ring model sets with exhaustive or window-pruned enumeration,
  graph-Laplacian modes, couplings.

Canonical complete core export barrel: `packages/core/src/index.ts`.

For a generic single-window `ModelSet`, `sample({ strategy:
'window-pruned', maxTraversalNodes, coefficientRanges })` uses exact
halfspace bounds to skip impossible coefficient prefixes. It returns the same
ordered `ModelPoint` records as the default `box` strategy and adds
`patch.enumeration` work evidence. `PenroseModelSet` remains a separate
coefficient-box sampler because its finite `C5` class selects among four
windows.

## Physics anchors

- Rigid: `massPropertiesFromCellComplex4`, `RigidBody4`, `PhysicsWorld4`,
  `RigidBodyObject4Binding`.
- Rigid collision/query: `HyperplaneColliderN`, `Hyperbox4`, support shapes,
  GJK, EPA, linear casts, narrowphase dispatch, named contact pipelines.
  `gjkDistance` reports `separated` only with a support-gap certificate and
  terminates under equal or nearly tied support directions; `iteration-limit`
  is an explicit refusal (a stable distance estimate is not a certificate),
  with `duplicate-support` naming a proved fixpoint refused early.
- Rigid constraints: point, distance, direction, orientation, planar rotation,
  motors, and bounded blocks.
- RN point/XPBD: `XpbdConstraintSolverN`, `XpbdParticleN`, `XpbdWorldN`,
  particle binding, distance-network, simplex-measure, StVK family, and
  particle--hyperplane contact families.
- Simplex constitutive references: `SimplexConstitutiveEvaluationN`,
  `evaluateSimplexStVenantKirchhoffN`, and
  `evaluateSimplexCompressibleNeoHookeanN`. The optional
  `evaluateSimplexMeasureBarrierN` / `simplexMeasureBarrierLawN` pair supplies
  a C2-clamped lower-measure energy and analytic gradient.
- Constitutive assembly: `SimplexConstitutiveLawN`, built-in immutable law
  descriptors, `compileSimplexConstitutiveFamilyN`, plus named StVK and
  Neo-Hookean family compilers.
- Exact constitutive curvature:
  `SimplexConstitutiveHessianVectorEvaluationN` and the three
  `evaluateSimplex*HessianVectorN` functions return matrix-free
  `Hessian(U) * direction`; capable families assemble the same optional
  provider seam by source vertex. This is not force-derivative sign, a dense
  Hessian, or a Newton policy.
- Matrix-free Newton direction:
  `solveXpbdIncrementalPotentialNewtonDirectionN` applies bounded
  preconditioned CG to the complete analytic incremental-objective operator.
  It returns explicit convergence, budget, unsupported-provider, and
  non-positive-curvature evidence. It does not select or apply a nonlinear
  step.
- Modified-Newton curvature:
  analytic composition, the Newton solve, and `xpbdNewtonDirectionPolicyN`
  accept `curvaturePolicy: { kind: 'provider-local-psd' }` or
  `{ kind: 'provider-block-psd' }`. The first reconstructs one dense Hessian
  per provider. The second uses an exact provider-authored additive block
  decomposition, or reports one `implicit-provider` fallback, and audits the
  raw block sum against the aggregate HVP. Simplex constitutive families
  declare one source-retained block per element. Both explicit CPU references
  audit symmetry, clamp negative eigenvalues, and retain spectra plus
  eigensystem diagnostics. Their cost is cubic in the complete provider or
  each declared block respectively; neither is a cached sparse large-mesh
  backend. Omission preserves exact curvature and typed refusal.
- Fixed-coordinate curvature:
  `compileXpbdIncrementalPotentialAnalyticHessianOperatorN` copies one packed
  coordinate and returns either a reusable analytic operator or a typed
  unsupported-provider refusal. Exact mode stays matrix-free. Provider-local
  and provider-block PSD pay basis HVPs and eigendecomposition once, then
  reuse stored projected matrices. Block-local application still pays one
  aggregate provider HVP per nonzero direction to audit the declared raw sum.
  The Newton CG solver uses this compiler once per linearization and reports
  construction and application provider-call counts separately. Nothing is
  cached across candidate coordinates or nonlinear iterations.
- Candidate objectives: `XpbdConservativeForceProviderN`, family
  `evaluateAt(positionOf)`, and `evaluateXpbdPotentialStateN` evaluate and
  assemble trial-state energy plus `dU/dx` without mutating live particles.
- Incremental objectives: `predictXpbdInertialStateN` constructs non-mutating
  inertial centers; `evaluateXpbdIncrementalPotentialN` returns
  `1/2 sum m||q-qHat||^2 + h^2 U(q)` and its free-coordinate gradient.
- Solver view: `compileXpbdIncrementalPotentialProblemN` packs dynamic
  particle axes; `searchXpbdIncrementalPotentialArmijoN` performs auditable
  sufficient-decrease backtracking. Only typed potential-domain trials are
  recoverable.
- Admissible steps: `XpbdIncrementalPotentialStepFilterN` certifies, limits,
  or explicitly refuses an initial particle-space search segment.
  `XpbdParticleHyperplaneBarrierStepFilterN` supplies the exact RN
  point-static-plane specialization and retains impact evidence.
- Finite source features: `XpbdParticleSourceSimplexBarrierN` evaluates
  unsigned point-to-closed-simplex distance while retaining the closest
  barycentric source coordinate. Pair it with
  `XpbdParticleSourceSimplexBarrierStepFilterN`, whose `certifiedFraction` is
  a conservative convexity/Lipschitz certificate, not an exact impact time.
  It does not generate mesh candidates or supply analytic provider curvature.
- Finite obstacle families:
  `compileXpbdParticleSourceSimplexBarrierFamilyN` combines an
  `XpbdParticleBindingN` with a separate static simplex group. It reports all
  possible pairs, conservative swept-AABB candidates, exact active barriers,
  and the blocking candidate of its paired aggregate step filter. Spread
  `...family.incrementalPotentialTerms()` into a problem or step. Candidate
  sets are valid only for the queried point/segment; this is an exhaustive CPU
  reference, not self-contact, moving--moving contact, or a spatial tree.
- Static convex-hull contact:
  `compileXpbdParticleSourceConvexHullBarrierFamilyN` represents the **convex
  hull of the obstacle vertices selected by `sourceGroup`** — the cells select
  vertices; they are *not* summed contact cells, and any concavity between the
  selected vertices is filled. One certified closest-point query per bound
  particle, one barrier force along the separation normal, and a
  source-retained witness naming the authoritative obstacle vertices behind
  the closest feature. Choose it over the per-simplex family when the cells
  merely decompose one solid: summing per-cell barriers there manufactures a
  decomposition-dependent tangential force, while one set query pushes along
  the support normal. The hull is static for the family's lifetime (moved
  coordinates are refused, never followed), proximity to a lower-dimensional
  hull is unsigned and two-sided, an undecided query is a typed
  `closest-point-indeterminate` refusal, and the paired filter's
  `maximumStepLength` is a certified prefix, not an impact time. Minimal
  recipe: compile with `binding`, `obstacle`, `sourceGroup`,
  `minimumDistance`, `activationDistance`, `stiffness`; spread
  `...family.incrementalPotentialTerms()` into a problem or step.
- Source-indexed contact barriers:
  `compileXpbdParticleHyperplaneBarrierFamilyN` reuses an
  `XpbdParticleHyperplaneFamilyN` source/particle/plane mapping and compiles
  paired per-vertex providers plus filters.
  Spread `...family.incrementalPotentialTerms()` into a problem or step, or
  pass existing terms to that method to append without mutating them.
- Reference minimization: `minimizeXpbdIncrementalPotentialN` uses an explicit
  packed direction policy and Armijo search under iteration, trial, and
  gradient-tolerance bounds. `xpbdSteepestDescentDirectionN` is the unchanged
  default; `xpbdMassPreconditionedDirectionN` scales each free-particle block
  by its exact inverse inertial mass. It returns converged, iteration-limit,
  line-search-exhausted, line-search-refused, or stalled evidence and retains
  its exact problem plus direction-policy identity.
- Atomic application: `applyXpbdIncrementalPotentialResultN` applies only a
  converged result after proving live-state and result-evidence freshness.
  Default dynamic velocity is `(qNext - qBefore) / h`; fixed velocity is
  preserved and external force clears. Refusals do not write partial state.
- Integrated reference step: `stepXpbdIncrementalPotentialN` composes
  prediction, compilation, bounded minimization, verification, and application.
  It retains each intermediate result and restores the complete pre-step
  particle state on typed refusal or thrown failure.
- Discrete cosine-fold bending: `compileXpbdSourceSimplexCosineBendingFamilyN`
  adds extrinsic stiffness over adjacent source simplices, with
  `evaluateSimplexHingeCosineN` as its pure per-hinge evaluator. The coordinate
  is `c = -uA . uB` over the shared-face conormals — the orientation-neutral
  cosine of the fold from flat, `1` flat and `-1` fully folded. **It is not a
  signed dihedral and not a shell model.** The energy `0.5 k (c - cRest)^2` is
  quartic in the fold angle, is not mesh-convergent (`~n^-2.99` under
  refinement), and its stiffness is discretization-dependent. Flat rest has a
  vanishing first derivative, so small folds respond weakly. Only unit
  weighting exists. First-order only: Newton-CG refuses the mixture with named
  unsupported-provider evidence. Always pass `family.stepFilter` alongside the
  provider — a segment can start and end valid while crossing zero conormal
  height in between, and only the filter sees that.
- Static-obstacle candidate acceleration: `compileXpbdSourceSimplexAabbHierarchyN`
  builds an immutable AABB tree over one static source-simplex obstacle. Select
  it by passing the compiled hierarchy as `candidateHierarchy` to
  `compileXpbdParticleSourceSimplexBarrierFamilyN`. Exhaustive search remains
  the default and the oracle; there is no `'fast'` string and no automatic
  switch by mesh size. The hierarchy must index the same `obstacle` and
  `simplexGroup` **objects** as the family. Candidate identities and their order
  are exactly the exhaustive ones, so only `diagnostics.strategy` and
  `diagnostics.hierarchy` reveal which ran. Retention is not contact: the exact
  P44 barrier and the paired step filter still decide. The obstacle must not
  move — the hierarchy snapshots its indexed coordinates and throws
  "the indexed obstacle moved" rather than rebuilding; compile a new one after
  moving the source. Worst-case work is linear, and the diagnostics report it.
- World-scoped entry point: `stepXpbdIncrementalPotentialWorldN` is the
  first-choice call when the scene is an authored `XpbdWorldN`. The world
  supplies `dimension`, `particles`, `gravity`, and the conservative provider
  registry; the caller supplies only the ordered `stepFilters`, `deltaTime`,
  and the warm-start/minimization/application policies. It delegates exactly
  once and returns `{ selection, step, diagnosis }`, where `step` is the
  unchanged lower-level result. Registered scalar constraints, velocity
  responses, state guards, and non-conservative force providers are named as
  configuration errors, never skipped; `deltaTime` must be finite and strictly
  positive.
- Open-domain initialization: the default remains `warmStart:
  'inertial-prediction'`; `'previous-positions'` uses the last live state.
  Opt-in `'feasible-inertial-prediction'` samples a bounded chord between them
  and retains `feasibleBaseRecovery` evidence. The standalone
  `recoverXpbdIncrementalPotentialFeasibleBaseN` exposes the same headless
  query. Neither API performs depenetration, nearest-point projection, or
  collision response, and measured iteration savings are scene-dependent.
- A measure barrier can be compiled as a second generic constitutive family on
  the same simplex group and exact particles. It is a proactive force, not an
  inversion guarantee; retain endpoint and signed/intrinsic chord guards.
- Accepted RN state: `XpbdStateGuardN`,
  `compileSimplexConstitutiveFamilyStateGuardN`,
  `analyzeLinearSimplexOrientationN`,
  `compileSimplexConstitutiveFamilyTrajectoryGuardN`,
  `analyzeLinearSimplexMeasureN`,
  `compileSimplexConstitutiveFamilyMeasureTrajectoryGuardN`, and bounded
  transactional `XpbdWorldN.stepAdaptive()`. Use the signed pair for an
  N-simplex in R^N and the intrinsic Gram-determinant pair for a k-simplex in
  R^N. Both certify only a linear substep chord and are not nonlinear barriers
  or formal interval-arithmetic proofs.
- RN velocity policies: `XpbdVelocityResponseN`,
  `compileXpbdParticleHyperplaneFrictionFamilyN` (complete Coulomb tangent
  ball), and `XpbdExponentialVelocityDampingN` (inverse-seconds decay).

Canonical complete physics export barrel: `packages/physics/src/index.ts`.
Candidate-state objective guide: `docs/learn/theory/candidate-potentials.md`.
Incremental objective guide: `docs/learn/theory/incremental-potentials.md`.

## Three anchors

- `ProjectedEdges3D`: projected 1-skeleton render product. Its options accept
  `color` or a complete `material`, not both; unknown keys such as `linewidth`
  are rejected because WebGL does not reliably implement line width.
- `ProjectedSurface3D`: projected 2-face mesh with source-triangle picking.
- `SlicedComplex3D`: exact 4D section from tetrahedral 3-cells.
- `SlicedComplex3D.triangleCount`: accessor, not a method; `0` means the cut
  missed the body entirely.
- Picking needs geometry and a ray, not a canvas: `update()` builds the
  `BufferGeometry`, and `product.object` is an ordinary `Mesh`, so a
  `Raycaster` works headlessly with no `WebGLRenderer`.
- `SlicedComplex3D.sourceCrossingsOfFace`: the retained source edge and
  parameter behind each corner of a section face. This is the crossing
  evidence, not a parent-cuboid reconstruction.
- `SlicedComplex3D.facesOfSourceTet`: current section faces produced by one
  source tetrahedron; useful for exact source-linked highlighting.
- `SlicedComplex3D.colorForTet` builds a palette once. Call
  `recolorBySourceTet()` explicitly when application state changes; `update()`
  does not reevaluate the callback.
- `HyperplaneSlice4.projectPointToChart`: orthogonally express an ambient R4
  point in a slice chart and retain the discarded signed normal distance.
  `embedPoint(coordinates)` recovers the original only when that distance is
  zero.
- `SampledSlicedField3D`, `FieldRelief3D`: field visualization products.
- `DragRotation4D`: pointer deltas → visual `Rotor4`, default Alt drag in xw/yw.
- `representationHitFrom…`: map a Three ray intersection to source-aware
  `RepresentationHitN`. An exact section hit's ambient point is in the posed
  ambient frame used for the product's latest update, not the unposed complex
  frame.

Canonical complete Three export barrel: `packages/three/src/index.ts`.

## Minimal, accurate patterns

```ts
// Project and slice the same R4 geometry. tetrahedralizeCuboidCells is the
// rendering-only path: it supplies the tetrahedral 3-cells a section needs and
// drops sourceCellIndices/permutationIndices. If a pick must name the parent
// cuboid, build the simplices with simplexizeCuboidGroupN and keep that map.
const complex = tetrahedralizeCuboidCells(createHypercube({ dim: 4, size: 2 }));
const pose = TransformN.identity(4);
const shadow = new ProjectedEdges3D(
  complex, new PerspectiveProjection({ fromDim: 4, viewDistance: 4 })
);
const section = new SlicedComplex3D(complex, HyperplaneSlice4.axisAligned(3, 0));
scene.add(shadow.object, section.object);
shadow.update(pose);
section.update(pose);
```

```ts
// Keep a slice slider inside the source's vertex-hull interval. The slice
// normal is normalized, so these values are in source units.
const range = cellComplexBoundsAlongDirectionN(complex, slice.normal, pose);
slice.offset = Math.max(range.min, Math.min(range.max, requestedOffset));
```

```ts
// Sweep a W slice; this is an exact cross-section, not a camera motion.
slice.offset = 0.8 * Math.sin(time);
slice.setNormal([0.15, 0, 0, 1]); // normalizes and keeps a continuous frame
section.update(pose);
```

```ts
// R4 physical angular velocity: coefficients are xy, xz, xw, yz, yw, zw.
body.setAngularVelocityWorld(BivectorN.fromPlanes(4, [
  { i: 0, j: 3, angle: 0.6 },
  { i: 1, j: 2, angle: -0.2 }
]));
world.step(1 / 120);
surface.update(new TransformN(4, body.rotation, body.position));
```

```ts
// Small-system Float64 golden path; this does not apply the result.
const result = minimizeXpbdIncrementalPotentialN({
  problem,
  initialCoordinates: problem.packPositions(candidatePositions),
  directionPolicy: xpbdMassPreconditionedDirectionN,
  gradientTolerance: 1e-8,
  maximumIterations: 128
});
if (result.status === 'converged') {
  inspectCandidate(result.final.positions);
}
```

```ts
// Explicit state transition; expected staleness is returned, not hidden.
const application = applyXpbdIncrementalPotentialResultN({
  result,
  velocityUpdate: 'backward-euler',
  clearForces: true
});
if (application.status === 'refused') {
  inspectRefusal(application);
}
```

```ts
// One-call conservative RN reference step with complete transaction evidence.
const step = stepXpbdIncrementalPotentialN({
  dimension: 4,
  particles,
  providers: [material, barrier],
  deltaTime: 1 / 120,
  gravity: [0, -9.81, 0, 0]
});
if (step.status === 'applied') {
  binding.writeSourcePositions();
}
```

```ts
// Discrete cosine-fold bending. The filter travels with the provider.
const bending = compileXpbdSourceSimplexCosineBendingFamilyN({
  id: 'membrane-bending',
  binding: membraneBinding,
  simplexGroup: membraneGroup,
  stiffness: 25,          // discretization-dependent; not a material constant
  restCoordinate: 1,      // flat
  minimumMeasureRatio: 0.05
});
const bendingTerms = bending.incrementalPotentialTerms();
```

```ts
// Same transaction, with the authored world as the single source of truth for
// dimension, particle order, gravity, and providers.
const advance = stepXpbdIncrementalPotentialWorldN({
  world,
  deltaTime: 1 / 120,
  stepFilters: contactTerms.stepFilters,
  warmStart: 'feasible-inertial-prediction'
});
if (advance.step.status === 'applied') {
  binding.writeSourcePositions();
} else {
  inspectRefusal(advance.diagnosis.condition, advance.diagnosis.levers);
}
```

```ts
// Pick a projected triangle. Identity, precision, and uniqueness are separate
// questions; a Three intersection is passed straight through.
const hit = representationHitFromProjectedSurface(surface, intersection);

useSourceCell(hit.source); // structural identity of the selected primitive

if (hit.ambientPointStatus === 'exact') {
  if (hit.ambiguity === 'none') {
    useUniqueAmbientPoint(hit.ambientPoint);
  } else {
    // Exact on the source triangle the ray named; the whole projection is
    // many-to-one, so this is not the pixel's source point.
    useSelectedPrimitivePoint(hit.ambientPoint, hit.ambiguity);
  }
}
```

## Avoid these invented APIs or assumptions

- `createSimplex`/`createCrossPolytope` stop at 3-cells BY DEFAULT; pass
  `maxCellDimension` for higher face families (simplex: through `dim`, the
  top cell; cross-polytope: through `dim - 1`, and a requested top cell
  refuses — it is not a simplex). Authored index order is combinatorial, NOT
  boundary-coherent: shared faces double, so render double-sided; oriented
  boundaries come from `sectionSimplexGroupN`, not from authored order.
- `@holotope/three` peer range is **`>=0.184.0 <0.186.0`**, and it is a
  *tested* interval (r183.0-r185.1 were all driven; r183 is excluded because
  `@types/three` is broken at 0.183.0 and missing at 0.183.2, not because the
  runtime failed). It is not a forward-compatibility promise. The development,
  showcase, and CDN reference stays exactly `three@0.185.1`: a peer window and
  a reproducibility anchor are different things, so do not "update" the pins to
  match the range. Never widen the range to make `pnpm check:three-compat`
  pass — that guard drives both ends from packed artifacts.
- Friction (P57) has FOUR distinctions that are load-bearing and routinely
  got wrong: (1) `XpbdParticleHyperplaneFrictionN` is the P16 **post-projection
  velocity response** for `world.step()`, while `XpbdSourceSimplexPairFrictionN`
  is a **term inside the incremental objective** — the optimizer refuses
  velocity responses on purpose and the second does not route around that;
  (2) the P57 term is conservative **only while one frozen lag is held**, not
  globally conservative — dissipation happens when the lag is refreshed;
  (3) **friction work is not generic backward-Euler energy decay** — an
  integrator can lose energy with `mu = 0`, so decay alone proves nothing and
  the work must be measured; (4) a P56 filter's **certified prefix is not a
  collision or friction-transition time**. Also: only a `separated-unique`
  pair may create a lag; a consumed lag is a named failure, never an implicit
  refresh; and the family's effective friction is **mesh-topology dependent**
  (shared edge 2x, four-cell refinement 4x), so a coefficient tuned on one
  mesh does not transfer to a refinement of it.
- Feature contact (P56): `evaluateSourceSimplexPairDistanceN`,
  `XpbdSourceSimplexPairBarrierN` + its step filter, and
  `compileXpbdSourceSimplexPairBarrierFamilyN`. Three warnings are load-
  bearing: (1) **point contact does not certify a surface** — every sheet
  vertex can be legally separated while a triangle interior is pierced, which
  is exactly what the pair query exists to see; (2) **a certified distance
  does not imply a unique differentiable witness** — `separated-multiple`
  carries every tied witness and no gradient, and the barrier refuses it by
  type; (3) **a filter's certified prefix is not a collision time** —
  `maximumStepLength` is a conservative Lipschitz bound, never an impact
  solve. Weights are in source vertex order on both sides; swapping the pair
  negates the direction and swaps the evidence. Four exclusions belong beside
  those warnings: this is **not** self-contact, **not** general mesh-mesh CCD,
  the family opposes **one static** feature (no moving-obstacle family), and
  there is **no friction or dissipation**. Overlapping source cells that share
  the contacted sub-feature each contribute a term naming the same witness, so
  effective contact stiffness follows local mesh topology.
- Do not call `PlaneEmbedding3D` a projection, and do not ask it for a fibre
  or a homogeneous matrix — it is injective, implements neither, and its
  lineage step is `plane-embedding`, never a projection kind. Do not upgrade
  a Float32 pick on an embedded image to `'exact'`; injectivity uniquifies
  the inverse of the exact image, not the observation.

- Do not expect a `PhysicsWorld4.addBody()` call alone to create collisions.
- Do not expect projected picks to always yield a unique R4 point.
- Do not create a `SlicedComplex3D` from a raw cuboid complex without the
  required tetrahedral 3-cells.
- Do not overlay a `SlicedComplex3D` on a projected product without passing
  that product's projection through `options.projection`. A section is
  expressed in the cutting hyperplane's own display frame, which is not the
  projection's output space. The two coincide at `offset: 0`, where the
  perspective scale is 1, and separate as the offset moves — about 14% at
  `w = 0.5` for `viewDistance: 4`. Either share the projection or show them as
  separate views.
- Do not call both `world.step()`/`world.stepAdaptive()` and
  `stepXpbdIncrementalPotentialWorldN()` for one physical interval. They are
  alternative solvers, not stages: projected XPBD applies the registered
  constraints, responses, and guards, while the optimization path cannot
  represent any of them and rejects their presence. Running both integrates
  the interval twice. Pick one per frame.
- Do not pass a bending provider to an incremental solve without its paired
  `stepFilter`, treat the cosine coordinate as a signed dihedral, expect
  mesh-convergent or transferable stiffness, or expect Newton-CG support.
- Do not treat a hierarchy-retained pair as contact, cache a candidate set
  across a changed point or segment, expect an automatic rebuild after moving
  the obstacle, assume sublinear worst-case work, or omit the paired step
  filter because a hierarchy exists. A different tree shape never changes
  source identity or candidate order.
- Do not treat `DragRotation4D` as physical angular velocity or torque.
- Do not guess exports: inspect the canonical barrel listed above when the
  needed feature is not in this file.
- Do not expect `tetrahedralizeCuboidCells` to replace the cuboid cells, or to
  retain the parent-cell map.
- Do not expect a `CellGroup` to report its own cell count, or cells to carry
  facet metadata; both are computed from `indices` and positions.
